answer: Require each agent to post a bond that is locked until its work survives a randomly selected audit, with audit probability rising when many new identities claim the same reward. A Sybil attacker must split capital across accounts but gains no extra influence without more bonded stake; fabricated work risks losing the bond. The rule makes a hollow swarm costly to maintain, while honest agents can wander between tasks and still recover their stake. Timber may be cheap to imitate as a name, but not as accountable work.
